newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to close all 5-and-10 stores - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to close all 5-and-10 stores - WSJ.

text.p: Woolworth Corp is expected to close its more than 400 F.W. Woolworth five-and-dime stores in the U.S. and record an after-tax charge of about $200 million to pay for costs associated with the move, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the paper said the announcement is expected Thursday.

The article said the decision by the retail giant ends a long attempt at squeezing profits from a business that accounts for more than $1 billion of the company's annual sales, which exceed $8 billion.
The move also ends an effort to bring the 117-year-old business into retailing's modern age, the story said.
Last year, the U.S. Woolworth stores reported an operating loss of $37 million and the losses have worsened this year, according to analysts' estimates, the story said.
It is not clear what would happen to the more than 9,000 full and part-time employees employed at the Woolworth division, the article said.
A Woolworth spokesperson declined comment, the story said.
The Journal said the information for the story came from people familiar with the plans.
